referents.why: 'Him' is the object of 'questioned', masculine singular. Jesus is the one questioned and the addressee of Pilate's speech.
'how many things' (posa) is an interrogative quantifier whose referent is the charges. No candidate in this verse is the charges.
'you' (genitive, against you) is second person inside Pilate's speech, so it is the addressee of that speech: Jesus.
'you' in 'Have you no answer?' is second person inside Pilate's speech: Jesus.
Third plural accusers, 'they are bringing charges'. The plural leaders of 15:1 and 15:3 are the referent; the elders composite is the plural candidate offered.

links.why: A clause cannot follow itself; the self-link is invalid.
The participle saying is nested in the questioning clause.
The speech is nested in the saying participle, as the grammar nests the object clause.
Clause cl3 is a second sentence of Pilate's speech, not nested in the role of cl2 (Have you no answer). Nothing nests it there.
The saying participle introduces Pilate's words. Per R1, added alongside the turn.
The second sentence (Look how many charges) is also Pilate's words under the same saying. Per R1.

none_fit.what: Two juxtaposed sentences of one speech with no conjunction: the second gives the charges that the question leans on. No link type says grounded in without a conjunction.
Repetition of Pilate's earlier questioning (Mrk.15.2#cl0). No link type marks 'again'.
An exclamation of notice ('look'), not a command to anyone; no group kind for a bare exclamation.
two sentences of one speech set side by side without a connective; no link type for juxtaposed sentences, the turn carries them

cant_tell.why: The chief priests are named in Mrk.15.1 but are not offered as a candidate here, and c8 is the only plural accuser listed. Chose c8 for now.
